name: Prion Protein Systemic Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence
Immunohistochemical or mass spectrometry identification of prion protein as amyloid fibril component
Evidence of systemic organ involvement (e.g., renal, cardiac, neurological) consistent with amyloidosis
Detection of pathogenic PRNP gene mutations associated with systemic amyloidosis
Exclusion of other common amyloid types (AL, AA, ATTR) by appropriate testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histological confirmation of amyloid deposits with prion protein identification plus evidence of systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; exclusion of other amyloidosis types is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy with amyloid deposits
searchTerms: sensory and motor nerve problems from amyloid

pathognomonic.symptomName: Nephrotic syndrome due to renal amyloid infiltration
searchTerms: nephrotic syndrome from amyloid in kidneys
restrictive heart disease due to protein deposits

common.symptomName: Orthostatic hypotension secondary to autonomic neuropathy
searchTerms: dizziness when standing due to nerve damage

common.symptomName: Gastrointestinal dysmotility including diarrhea and malabsorption
Carpal tunnel syndrome from amyloid deposition
searchTerms: carpal tunnel symptoms due to deposits

occasional.symptomName: Cutaneous purpura due to vascular amyloid deposits
searchTerms: skin bruising from blood vessel deposits
purple skin spots due to amyloid
low thyroid hormone due to amyloid

rare.symptomName: Vitreous opacities due to ocular amyloid deposits

searchTerms: enlarged liver with high liver enzymes
bleeding tendency due to weak blood vessels

laboratory: Proteinuria with nephrotic range protein loss
Elevated serum creatinine in renal involvement
Abnormal serum free light chains excluded
Elevated NT-proBNP and troponin in cardiac amyloidosis
imaging: Echocardiogram showing restrictive cardiomyopathy with thickened ventricular walls
MRI with late gadolinium enhancement in cardiac amyloid infiltration
Nerve conduction studies showing sensorimotor polyneuropathy
other: Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence on biopsy specimens
Mass spectrometry confirming prion protein as amyloid fibril component

distinguishingFeatures: More common cardiac involvement with rapid progression
TTR gene mutations or wild-type transthyretin deposits
Different amyloid fibril protein on mass spectrometry

redFlags: Nephrotic syndrome with unexplained amyloid deposits
Progressive sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy with systemic signs
